item.text:
**Assessment:** mostly yes. Scholz’s 2024 record is strongly pro-investment, pro-startup, and pro-capital-markets, with repeated calls to cut bureaucracy and improve financing conditions. The main counterweight is not cronyism or expropriation, but late-2024 political collapse that weakened predictability and implementation.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Other IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Support | Agreement on 2025 budget and growth initiative | Federal Government | 2024-07-05 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/budget-2025-2298116 | Scholz said the budget and growth initiative would keep the debt limit, give tax relief, expand infrastructure and renewables, and support stronger growth. That is a clear attempt to set fair, growth-oriented rules for investment and job creation. | 5B.4, 5B.1, 5B.3 |
| Support | "Jede Idee, die uns voranbringt, ist wertvoll" | Federal Government | 2024-10-24 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/interview-vcm-2317400 | Scholz said the start-up strategy already had 130 measures, 80% implemented, and that Germany needed better venture-capital financing and new savings/investment incentives. This is direct evidence of rules designed to help entrepreneurship and scale-up finance. | 5B.4, 5B.1 |

That is strong pro-entrepreneurship rule-setting. | 5B.4, 5B.1, 5B.3 |

This is not evidence of anti-market favoritism, but it is real counterevidence on predictable rule-making. | 5B.4, 4B.10, 5B.3 |

That weakens continuity and predictability for entrepreneurs and investors, even if it does not show cronyism or property-rights abuse. | 5B.4, 4B.10, 5B.3 |

Search gap: I found **no direct evidence** of Scholz using property-rights violations, arbitrary expropriation, favoritism toward specific business partners, or anti-competitive capture. The main negative evidence is **instability and incomplete implementation**, not overtly unfair market rules.
